Consult Summary:
- Telephone triage for acute neurologic deficits: sudden inability to move left arm on waking (~1 hour prior), left facial tingling, dysphagia, and speech difficulty; high suspicion for acute stroke. Emergency ambulance arranged for transport to Emergency Department; patient instructed to unlock door and wait by entry.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden inability to move left arm upon waking today.
- Timeline:
  - Onset: On waking, approximately 1 hour prior to call.
  - Course: Persistent during call; patient reports speech getting “a bit harder” as call progressed.
- Symptoms:
  - Left arm: Complete inability to move; no pain; no discoloration; not cold.
  - Face: Tingling on the left side since onset.
  - Swallowing: Difficulty swallowing.
  - Speech: Feels slower/harder; requires more effort to speak; no explicit slurred speech described; patient notes increased difficulty over time.
  - Legs: No symptoms in left leg.
  - Face symmetry: Patient has not noticed facial asymmetry.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Denies sleeping in awkward position or different bed; no known triggers.
- Prior episodes: None reported.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Hypertension.
- Allergies: Penicillin.
- Medications:
  - Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Losartan — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Amlodipine — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Tobacco: Former smoker.
- Alcohol: “A few drinks over the weekend” and “a couple more during the week,” primarily beer (pints).
- Safety: Advised to unlock front door and wait in hallway for EMS access; patient compliant.

Family History:
- Father: Heart disease (details not known).
- No other family history reported.

Physical Examination:
- Telemedicine (telephone) encounter; no visual assessment possible.
- No vitals obtained.
- Neurologic exam not performed due to phone format; symptoms as per patient report.

Investigations:
- None performed during call. Plan for emergency hospital evaluation and stroke team assessment.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute neurologic deficit — suspected acute cerebrovascular event (possible stroke)
  - Assessment: Sudden onset left arm paralysis, left facial tingling, dysphagia, and progressive speech difficulty beginning on waking approximately 1 hour before call; no trauma; high vascular risk profile (hypertension, type 2 diabetes); no arm pain, discoloration, or coolness.
  - Plan:
    - Emergency response initiated: Ambulance called to patient’s home for immediate transport to Emergency Department.
    - Instructions: Unlock front door; sit in hallway near entry to ensure access; remain on phone until EMS arrival.
    - Anticipated ED actions as discussed: Stroke physician assessment and consideration of acute stroke treatments.
    - Monitoring: Clinician remained on the line with patient until EMS arrival (as stated during call).

- General plan items:
  - No outpatient medications adjusted during this triage call.
  - No further instructions provided beyond safety and emergency transfer.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Exact time last known well; exact wake time; glucose level; blood pressure and other vitals; in-person neurologic exam (e.g., facial droop, strength grading, NIHSS); anticoagulant/antiplatelet use history; history of atrial fibrillation or prior stroke/TIA; headache, vision changes, gait/balance issues, seizure activity, head/neck trauma; medication doses/route/frequency; weight; code status/advance directives.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor hesitations/uncertainties in patient phrasing; telephone-only limitations noted.
